findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. This part works well.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: This is Athena's home URL, but the title and heading are about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena will first think they are on the wrong page. Only the lede shows that the page is a demonstration.

The second section is an error message. It sits in the place meant to prove Athena's main promise: tracing models, verdict and cost. A newcomer's first piece of evidence is a failure, which undercuts trust in the tool.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: A newcomer is not an owner, and nothing says whose proposals these are or why the link is in the header. It distracts from the real next step.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The header links straight to the next steps, so a newcomer does not have to scroll through the long firstmate study to find out how to act.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself.

findings.text: The install path is concrete: prerequisites, clone, ./setup.sh and a first command. The page does not mention that Claude Code needs an account or API access, and it does not say which systems are supported. A newcomer may hit these surprises during setup.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm (to install Claude Code)." ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: Most of the page is a dense state-machine analysis of firstmate. That suits someone who uses firstmate. A newcomer to Athena gets little from it beyond the impression that Athena is thorough, and it hides the Next steps section near the bottom.
findings.source: States of a piece of work / Transitions (t1–t12) / Claims and sources (c1–c45)

findings.text: Several glossary entries say plainly that a term is not defined in the source. That is honest, but it leaves a newcomer with jargon they cannot fully decode.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." / "does not define a durable record" / "does not define an endpoint" / "does not define a heartbeat"

findings.text: The page never names which models are used. It also never says what an Athena run costs. A newcomer weighing whether to try it has no rough figure.
findings.source: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost"

findings.text: This section describes Athena's internal repository layout. It means nothing to a newcomer who has not cloned the repository.
findings.source: About this page: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
